title: Maximal Torus Weight Orbits in a Finite Symplectic Group
body_html:
Maximal Torus Weight Orbits in a Finite Symplectic Group

Let \((E,j)\) be a symplectic vector space over \(k\), let \(S\) be its symplectic group, and let \(T\) be a maximal \(k\)-torus of \(S\). Over an algebraic closure, the action of \(T\) gives a weight decomposition \[ E=\bigoplus_{\epsilon\in P(E,T)} E^\epsilon . \]

The Galois group \(\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(\bar{k}/k)\) permutes the weights. For a Galois orbit \(\omega\), the sum \[ E^\omega=\bigoplus_{\epsilon\in \omega}E^\epsilon \] is defined over \(k\). The symplectic form pairs \(E^\epsilon\) with \(E^{-\epsilon}\), so the relevant blocks are indexed by orbits \[ \Omega=\{\omega,-\omega\}. \]

The orbit \(\omega\) is symmetric if \(\omega=-\omega\), and nonsymmetric otherwise.

For a nonsymmetric block, \(E^\Omega=E^\omega\oplus E^{-\omega}\), the two summands are dual, and the corresponding stabilizer is a general linear group over a finite extension \(k_\Omega/k\).

For a symmetric block, \(E^\Omega\) is naturally a one-dimensional skew-hermitian space over a quadratic extension \(K_\Omega/k_\Omega\), and the corresponding stabilizer is a finite unitary group.

In odd characteristic, Gérardin attaches to each block a distinguished nontrivial real character \(x_\Omega^T\) of \(T(k)\). The product of these block characters is the torus character \(X_T\) that appears in the semisimple character formula.
